body: This problem doesn't exist in v0.5.1, so this is a regression.

The problem seems to happen if the inserted character occupies a different number of bytes than the following multibyte character. For example, if the line contains one 2-byte character, then inserting a 1-byte character or a 3-byte character before it will cause an error, but inserting a 2-byte character before it will not.

We're seeing the same issue with the Lean language server when inserting a space before `⟨` (which encodes into 3 bytes of UTF-8).  Interestingly, this results in an LSP message which is not valid UTF-8:
```
Content-Length: 270

{"method":"textDocument\/didChange","params":{"contentChanges":[{"text":" <E2><9F>","rangeLength":0,"range":{"end":{"line":0,"character":0},"start":{"line":0,"character":0}}}],"textDocument":{"uri":"file:\/\/\/home\/gebner\/lean4\/scratch5.lean","version":5}},"jsonrpc":"2.0"}
```
I have escaped the malformed bytes. The actual bytes between the quotes in the text field is `"\x20\xe2\x9f"` (encoding `⟨` gives `"\xe2\x9f\xa8"`).

issue.body:
I'm about to head out for the evening, so this may be an easy fix, but the infoview seems to break totally if in Lean 3 I have a line like:

```lean
variables {𝔽 : Type*} {
```

Save that to a file, open it, and just append to the end of the line, and the traceback says:

```
Error detected while processing CursorMovedI Autocommands for "<buffer=1>":                                                                                                                     
E5108: Error executing lua /Users/julian/Development/lean.nvim/lua/lean/infoview.lua:545: index out of range                                                                                    
stack traceback:                                                                                                                                                                                
        [C]: in function 'str_byteindex'                                                                                                                                                        
        /Users/julian/Development/lean.nvim/lua/lean/infoview.lua:545: in function 'update_extmark'                                                                                             
        /Users/julian/Development/lean.nvim/lua/lean/infoview.lua:531: in function 'set_position_params'                                                                                        
        /Users/julian/Development/lean.nvim/lua/lean/infoview.lua:624: in function 'move'                                                                                                       
        /Users/julian/Development/lean.nvim/lua/lean/infoview.lua:443: in function 'move_pin'                                                                                                   
        /Users/julian/Development/lean.nvim/lua/lean/infoview.lua:846: in function '__update'                                                                                                   
        [string ":lua"]:1: in main chunk                                                                                                                                                        
```

(This obviously occurs when that line is in the middle of a longer file as well, and persists, so it basically just breaks the infoview).

It's still odd to me to see anything talking about pin updating when no pins are being used -- it seems something is miscalculating a character (which may be an easy fix), but in general I'd love it if no pin updates occurred unless I try to use pins.

More generally we probably should wrap infoview update calls in `pcall` and catch any failures and render them into the infoview so at least they don't repeatedly disrupt typing.

body:
@mjlbach I've identified the original problem causing #16352 in the Lua stdlib as [a faulty cast of `offset` to `char_u` in `str_utf_start()`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/bdfea9d9ae2b1db03c9cad9b0b07330b6f09cfa2/src/nvim/lua/stdlib.c#L233), which explains why we were seeing an issue exactly at the 256 byte boundary.

I don't yet have much experience with the C code, so lmk if this is an easy fix for you, but I see you're taking a (well-deserved) break so I can look into fixing this over the next few days.
@rish987 you could try changing it from `(char_u)` to `(ptrdiff_t)`. Or perhaps nothing, I think `PTR + long` should be considered well-defined anyways.
